news.text: 8 December saw the leaders of Russia (Boris Yeltsin), Ukraine (Leonid Kravchuk), and Belarus (Stanislav Shushkevich) meet secretly at a hunting lodge in the Belovezhskaya Pushcha forest to sign the historic **Belovezha Accords**. Declaring that the Soviet Union as a subject of international law had 'ceased to exist', the three founding republics formed the **Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)**, delivering the formal death blow to the **USSR**.
news.youtube: Belovezha Accords signing December 1991 USSR dissolution

news.text: 9 December saw leaders of the twelve European Community member states convene in the Netherlands to finalize negotiations on the historic **Maastricht Treaty**. Establishing the modern **European Union**, the landmark accord introduced the roadmap toward a single European currency (the euro), common foreign and security policies, and official European citizenship under a **three-pillar institutional structure**.
news.youtube: Maastricht Treaty summit negotiations December 1991 news

news.text: 15 December saw Queen's operatic masterpiece ***Bohemian Rhapsody*** re-enter the UK Singles Chart at number one following the tragic death of frontman Freddie Mercury. Released as a double A-side with *These Are the Days of Our Lives* to raise funds for the Terrence Higgins Trust AIDS charity, the classic single spent five weeks at the summit, becoming the first song ever to top the **UK Christmas charts** in **two separate decades**.

25 December saw Soviet President **Mikhail Gorbachev** deliver a televised address resigning from office and declaring the formal dissolution of the **Union of Soviet Socialist Republics**. At 7:32 pm Moscow time, the iconic red Soviet hammer-and-sickle flag was lowered over the Kremlin for the final time, replaced by the white, blue, and red tricolour of the Russian Federation, formally ending the **Cold War**.
news.youtube: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns Soviet flag lowered Kremlin December 25 1991

news.text: 29 December saw World Championship Wrestling stage ***Starrcade 1991*** before 9,000 fans at the Norfolk Scope in Virginia. Centred around the unique "Lethal Lottery" concept where random tag teams competed to qualify for the final 20-man two-ring battle royal, legendary powerhouse **Sting** eliminated Lex Luger to win the coveted **Battlebowl Battle Royal ring**.

gaming.title: Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge
gaming.reviewQuote: Funner, bigger, and infinitely more gorgeous than the original. The iMUSE dynamic musical score and hand-painted 256-colour art are pure wizardry.
gaming.headline: Big Whoop, Voodoo Dolls, and the iMUSE Musical Revolution
gaming.gameplay: Written and directed by **Ron Gilbert** alongside co-writers Tim Schafer and Dave Grossman, *Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge* debuted for MS-DOS in December 1991. Guiding aspiring pirate **Guybrush Threepwood** across Scabb, Phatt, and Booty Islands in search of the mythical treasure of Big Whoop, players navigated devilishly clever inventory puzzles, constructed a voodoo doll to neutralize the resurrected zombie pirate LeChuck, and participated in the infamous spitting competition. Crucially, the game debuted the **iMUSE interactive music engine**, blending seamless live musical transitions between scenes.
gaming.reception: Critics greeted the sequel with universal adoration. Publications lauded Peter Chan's hand-painted, storybook 256-colour VGA backgrounds, Michael Land and Clint Bajakian's adaptive reggae-infused soundtrack, and Gilbert's subversive, fourth-wall-shattering carnival climax, hailing it as the undisputed pinnacle of the graphic adventure genre.
gaming.impact: Consistently celebrated as one of the finest comedy games and graphic adventures ever created, *Monkey Island 2* pushed computer storytelling, dynamic soundtrack composition, and point-and-click logic to their absolute historic zenith.
